title: BEACON: Cross-Domain Co-Training of Generative Robot Policies via Best-Effort Adaptation
claim: Abundant source data and scarce target data are combined through alternating policy training and importance reweighting, yielding a policy deployed on the target domain.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, data inputs, central optimization module, deployment photos at right
description: The figure reads left to right in three stages. On the left, a Source Data block (a robot arm drawing, a dot grid in yellow-green, and a box saying 'Large number of demos, Dense coverage') sits above a Target Data block (a real robot photo, a sparser teal dot grid, and a box saying 'Limited number of demos, Sparse coverage'). Chevron arrows lead into a large gray central panel. The panel's upper half shows a 'Policy Training' box with observation and action token sequences around a small encoder-decoder diagram. Beside it are the words 'Alternating Optimization', a double-headed curved arrow and 'Weight Update', and a balance-scale icon. Below a divider, 'Importance Reweighting' shows yellow and teal scatter boxes, with dots resized after reweighting. A final chevron points to a teal-bordered panel with two real-robot deployment photos labeled 'Deployment on Target Domain'. Yellow-green marks source data and teal marks target data throughout.
caption: The BEACON framework. Given a large amount of (multi-)source demonstrations and a small amount of target demonstrations, BEACON jointly learns a diffusion-based visuomotor policy and a set of per-sample weights using a discrepancyaware objective inspired by BEA.
abstract: We introduce BEACON--Best-Effort Adaptation for Cross-Domain Co-Training--a theory-guided framework for training generative robot policies with abundant source demonstrations and limited target demonstrations. BEACON casts cross-domain co-training as a discrepancy-aware importance-reweighting problem, jointly learning a diffusion-based visuomotor policy and per-sample source weights through an objective inspired by the Best-Effort Adaptation (BEA) bound. To make this approach practical for high-dimensional sequence policies, we develop scalable instance-level discrepancy proxies, stochastic alternating updates for policy and weights, and a multi-source extension that balances heterogeneous source domains. Across sim-to-sim, sim-to-real, and multi-source manipulation settings, BEACON improves robustness and data efficiency over target-only, fixed-ratio co-training, and feature-alignment baselines. Without an explicit alignment objective, BEACON also brings source and target representations closer together as an implicit result of discrepancy-aware co-training.
